title: LiPNet: a liver perfusion network model of haemodynamic load in partial liver grafts
description: LiPNet treats the liver as a dissipation-optimal perfusion network and derives three donor-normalised loads on a partial graft: the flow load zF (portal flow per 100 g relative to the donor), the pressure load zP (portocaval gradient over 5 mmHg) and the resistance load zR, related by zP = zF × zR. The archive holds the network model (2D and 3D graphs, closed-form scaling, allometric closure, exhaustive certificate on seven lobules), a lobule-scale finite-element layer, the provenance-labelled extraction of 31 groups from 17 published living donor liver transplantation series, the patient-level tables recovered from three of them, the hierarchical binomial model of outcome on pressure load with its sensitivity, validation and ecological-bias analyses, the sweep of the normalisation references behind zR, the code that reproduces every figure, and a browser calculator. The effect of changing the gradient is estimated within study; the absolute level of risk is centre-specific. Research tool, not a medical device.
